backbone: Reduce asphericity to contracting the spherical-coset poset; add cosets in a well-order by a harmonic height from a categorical Artin action, showing every earlier link empty or contractible.
quote: We add the vertices in a well-order. A vertex's \emph{earlier link} is the part of its link already present, and a \emph{source} has empty earlier link.

backbone: Uniform bounded-height theorem for self-quasi-isometries (volume-growth comparisons, compactness limits) turns the quasi-action into a homomorphism whose kernel has polynomial growth; Gromov and finiteness properties give polycyclicity.
quote: Transporting the left translation action of $H$ across a quasi-isometry gives maps of $G$ with uniform quasi-isometry bounds that respect multiplication up to a uniformly bounded error.

backbone: A kernel relation yields a planar surface of word disks; a multi-block fixed-space theorem (cohomological intersection) plus spectral-phase subadditivity forces every boundary word, hence the coefficient, trivial.
quote: The proof estimates one unitary operator in two ways. Mixing disks of the same type gives an upper bound for its phase. Reading the operator around the boundary gives an exact phase formula.

backbone: Sample a random nested-table presentation: with probability tending to one it is aspherical with linear filling, and any geometric CAT(0) action yields a limiting configuration forcing an impossible flat square.
quote: The proof is an existence argument and does not give an effective size for $K$.

backbone: Induction along the Magnus-Moldavanskii hierarchy; each HNN step is hyperbolic by a combination theorem whose annular flaring is proved by contradiction using stationary currents and Brinkmann expansion.
quote: The Freiheitssatz makes an inductive approach possible: a Magnus splitting has a smaller one-relator vertex group and free edge groups.

backbone: Explicit amalgam of a rank-100 free group with a direct product: a height-extension graphing gives cost near one, while a Bernoulli-to-rank transfer and deterministic rank bound give cost bounded away from one.
quote: We construct a finitely generated group with two essentially free probability-measure-preserving actions of different costs.

backbone: Prepare the asymptotic end, construct a filled graph/conformal deformation with controlled scalar curvature, mass and enclosing area, apply the Riemannian minimizing-frontier Penrose inequality, then pass to limits.
quote: The numerical argument first prepares the end, then performs one filled graph and conformal deformation.

backbone: Rare resonant cells and a hierarchy of increasingly sparse ports define a limiting affine scattering energy; 2D capacity forces it to vanish, a bootstrap yields fractional moments, Simon-Wolff gives pure point.
quote: The second ingredient is a comparison along a hierarchy of increasingly sparse ports

backbone: Lower-triangular combinations of trial eigenfunctions plus a matrix field path (endpoint via degree argument) give a finite-interval action inequality; an integrated matrix trace comparison recovers the sharp eigenvalue-moment bound.
quote: The action subtracts a power of the matrix density $\rho(x)=A(x)A(x)^{\mathsf T}$, and a complementary lower bound recovers the sum of the chosen eigenvalue moments.

backbone: Local Thomas-Fermi screening comparisons via noisy observations, then a positive comparison field is continued outward layer by layer, bounding electrons outside a terminal region and hence the excess charge.
quote: Finally, a positive comparison field is continued outward. A local maximum chooses between a shifted nonlinear subsolution and a shifted observed field.

backbone: Baire category: future extendible data are covered by countably many closed tests, each nowhere dense because explicit perturbations propagate a curvature signal forcing transport/holonomy failure near the Cauchy horizon.
quote: Here we prove a local, Baire-category form of this assertion near each fixed rotating subextremal Kerr bridge, at the threshold of locally square-integrable connection coefficients.

backbone: Gap gives an initial subvolume box exponent; replica/transport norm comparisons scanning collars improve it repeatedly to small collar information; ordered tile families and the entropy chain rule give the area law.
quote: The two norm bounds first improve the box exponent repeatedly; their sharper form then gives

backbone: Three MUBs exist classically; a certified computer-verified finite cover of all second bases by seed and phase balls, with local exclusion of two further bases in each, rules out four.
quote: Its upper bound combines that exhaustive cover with local exclusion of two further bases and the complete execution and arithmetic contract of Theorem~\ref{execute:finite-theorem}.

backbone: Write condensate fraction as an overlap of square-root Gibbs kernels; Brownian path representation and short-path comparison moving one particle through sparse obstacles give a volume-independent positive lower bound.
quote: We prove the needed thermal estimates and retain the deterministic comparison mechanism.

backbone: Express partition functions as moments of a spatial transfer operator; certified finite thermal computations give initial purities, and a coupled purity bootstrap doubling chain length yields a uniform gap.
quote: This gives a pair of initial purity defects at length $36$; six rounded updates then reach length $2304$.

backbone: Prove H^2 >= gamma H by comparing two-, three- and four-body terms with an explicit rotation-averaged positive sum of squares, verified by an exact rational certificate plus a finite-sphere error bound.
quote: It starts from the normal-ordered expansion of \(H_Q^2\). It has two-, three-, and four-body terms. We compare them with the corresponding terms of a positive operator

backbone: Simultaneous induction on N: compare the kernel with a massive deformation of Fredholm index p(N); profile decomposition and compactness assign p(N)-1 lines to proper clusters, leaving exactly one.
quote: Induction on the internal blocks and the permutation symmetries then give one line for each of the $p(N)-1$ proper partitions.

backbone: Random-loop (interchange) representation with pinned returns; a pin bootstrap and long-return bounds reduce the deficit to heat-kernel return sums of the dispersion walk, then pins represent field to obtain magnetization.
quote: Our proof therefore estimates the observable through a representation that remains uniform under arbitrary extra up-spin constraints, and only then passes to pressure increments.

backbone: Explicit PPT-composition state in dimension ten with an exact computer-checked certificate of no product vectors; a coherence inequality shows any admitted protocol output stays far from an ideal secret bit.
quote: We construct an entangled state for which even one approximately secret bit is uniformly out of reach.

backbone: Assume a strictly violating pair; fix thermal references, minimize a penalized entropy combination, and use Stieltjes interpolation plus stationarity identities to force the regularized minimizers thermal, contradiction.
quote: We fix those thermal reference parameters near a hypothetical strictly violating pair. This turns the contradiction into a negative minimum of a linear combination of three entropies

backbone: Localization of conjugated product projections by a finite backward induction on mismatch thresholds using Chebyshev polynomial approximations and inverse circuits; localization then contradicts parity advantage.
quote: A finite chain of thresholds ends above the maximum possible count $N$, where localization is automatic; working backward proves the original statement

backbone: Deterministic reduction from a QMA-complete lattice Heisenberg problem: place unit nuclei realizing tuned wells, derive Hubbard/Heisenberg effective model by perturbation bounds, and exclude lower-energy continuum states.
quote: A deterministic classical polynomial-time reduction produces polynomially many nuclei at distinct rational positions and polynomially many electrons, with polynomial rational bit lengths and threshold separation at least one.

backbone: A zero-block entropy inequality yields a thermal block inequality; peeling one qubit at a time and convexity give a population-sensitive output entropy bound, iterated over the block to obtain additivity.
quote: For a damping tensor power, convexity of $e$ combines the conditional populations into the original site populations, and iteration gives \eqref{eq:roadmap} without restricting the input vector.

backbone: Transfer lemma (proved by contradiction via tested-coordinate selection) converts Song's conditioning estimate into an exponential threshold bound for repeated entangled games.
quote: We obtain this theorem by combining a transfer from conditioning bounds to threshold bounds with Song's conditioning estimate~\cite[Lemma~4.4]{song2026}.

backbone: Explicit three-electron two-centre molecule; nodal-plane asymptotics of its density are incompatible, via translated-limit compactness and a weighted trace contradiction, with any noninteracting ensemble potential.
quote: We construct a finite three-electron Coulomb molecule whose spin-summed ground-state density cannot be reproduced by any ground-state ensemble of noninteracting electrons

backbone: Explicit circuit family: an order-finding trial with exactly prescribed dyadic success probability, verifiable transition data, equalization and one exact amplification step make factoring succeed with certainty.
quote: We construct a trial whose probability of returning the true order is an explicit dyadic function of that order.

backbone: Energy bounds from C2-cofiniteness give strong locality; annulus estimates integrate unitary modules; fusion positivity and a permutation-orbifold argument unitarize all modules; cited comparison theorems give the tensor equivalence.
quote: The central ordering issue is that a positive form on $V$ does not initially give positive forms on its modules or fusion products. We first work with modules already carrying such forms.

backbone: Take a near-optimal bounded classical Gaussian formula (Parisi/full-support input) and compile it into a fixed QAOA word via tree calculus and seeded controls, then remove seeds; limits give energy P*.
quote: The quantum construction simulates a finite classical calculation, using temporary Gaussian seed controls and then removing them.

backbone: Null-cut modular generators and Ward identities yield a scalar comparison; positivity forces critical tail and residual dilation charge to vanish, extracting a dimension-two scalar that improves the stress tensor.
quote: Actual diamond modular transformations extract a dimension-two scalar wave $S$ from the physical virial field, with real localization and bounded approximants in the original net.

backbone: Explicit uniform oracle circuit: transform the target to a block with small corner, encode a smaller unitary via truncated geometric-series Fourier fields, recurse, and compile all slots into one Boolean oracle.
quote: For that purpose we construct two maps, $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal R$, from the original space into a register holding $Z$ together with a smaller state.

backbone: Construct total functions with Forrelation-certified column certificates and outward pointers; a quantum tournament search gives the upper bound and a planted-input direct-product argument gives the randomized lower bound.
quote: We construct a total function whose accepting certificate belongs to one column.
